extraction_text: Ten warriors from the Kaurava side, including Bhurishravas, Kripa, Shalya, Satyaki, the Avanti brothers Vinda and Anuvinda, Jayadratha, Chitrasena, Vikarna, and the young Durmukha, fight against Bhima.

Shalya shoots nine arrows at Bhima, Satyaki shoots three, Kripa shoots nine, Chitrasena, Vikarna, and Bhurishravas each shoot ten crescent-headed arrows, Jayadratha hits Bhima's collarbone with three arrows, Vinda and Anuvinda each shoot five arrows, and Durmukha shoots twenty sharp arrows.
The mighty Bhima shoots many arrows at all these famous Kaurava warriors.
Bhima shot 105 arrows at Shalya, 8 at Shalya's brother, 1 at Kripa's bow, then 5 more after breaking it.
Bhima shot 3 arrows each at Vinda and Anuvinda, 30 at Duhshasana, 5 at Karna.
Bhima shot 10 arrows at Vikarna, 5 at Shalya's brother, then 3 more at Shalya's brother, causing Bhima to cheer.

Bhima, hit by many arrows, angrily shot many arrows back at Kripa in battle.

Shalya's brother, with broken bow, dead horses, slain charioteer, and disabled chariot, quickly boarded Karna's chariot.
Bhima shot arrows and blocked warriors, disabling Shalya's brother's chariot, creating a battle miracle.
Shalya, unable to bear Bhima's valor, shot 70 arrows at Bhima, shouting 'Stop! You stop!'
Kripa, Shalya's brother, Bhurishrava, Karna, Vinda, Anuvinda, Duhshasana, Vikarna, and Shalya's brother quickly shot at Bhima to support Shalya.
Bhima shot back 5 arrows at each of them and 70 at Shalya, then 10 more.
Shalya shot 9 arrows at Bhima, then 5 more, then 1 crescent-headed arrow deeply hitting Bhima's charioteer's vital spot.
Bhima, seeing his charioteer hit and injured, shot 3 arrows at Shalya's arms and chest.
Bhima shot 3 straight-flying arrows at each great archer and roared like a lion.
The great archers each shot 3 sharp-tipped arrows at Bhima's vital spots as he fought fiercely.
Bhima, severely wounded, remained unshaken like a mountain enduring a cloud's heavy rain.
Bhima shot 9 arrows fiercely at Shalya and 100 at Bhurishrava.
Bhima skillfully shot a sharp razor arrow, breaking Shalya's brother's bow with arrows.
Shalya's brother took another bow and shot an iron arrow at Bhima's forehead.
Bhima shot 9 iron arrows at Shalya, 3 at Bhurishrava, and 8 at Shalya's brother.
Bhima was attacked by multiple warriors including Drona, Kripa, Shalya, Jayadratha, and Sudakshina, who shot arrows and threw weapons at him.
Bhima skillfully defended himself, breaking Sudakshina's golden dart, shattering Jayadratha's spear and trident, destroying Kripa's weapon, and cutting Shalya's arrows.
Arjuna arrived on the battlefield and saw Bhima fighting.
Duryodhana urged Shalya to kill Arjuna and Bhima.
Shalya, along with his army, charged at Arjuna and Bhima, surrounding Arjuna with thousands of chariots.
Arjuna, in battle, shot arrows at Shalya, Shalya, Kripa, Sudakshina, and Jayadratha.
Arjuna also shot arrows at Karna, Vikarna, Duhshasana, and the two warriors from Avanti.
Jayadratha, standing on Karna's chariot, shot arrows at Arjuna and then at Bhima.
Shalya and Kripa repeatedly shot deadly arrows at Arjuna.
Duryodhana's sons, led by Karna, fought in the battle.
Shakuni and other warriors rapidly fired five sharp arrows each at Arjuna and Bhima.
Arjuna and Bhima, the sons of Kunti and excellent charioteers, attacked the army of Trigarta.
Shakuni shot an iron arrow at Arjuna with a powerful roar that echoed in the sky.
Other brave charioteers shot straight-flying, sharp gold-feathered arrows at Bhima and Arjuna.
Arjuna and Bhima, handsome with excellent chariots, moved among the charioteers like two powerful lions hunting among cattle.
Arjuna and Bhima repeatedly cut the bows and arrows of warriors and severed hundreds of heads.
Many chariots were destroyed, hundreds of horses killed, and elephants and elephant-riders fell in the great battle.
Duryodhana, terrified seeing Bhima and Arjuna united, approached Bhishma's chariot.
Kripa, Ashwatthama, Jayadratha (King of Sindhu), Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti joined the battle.
Bhima and Arjuna fiercely scattered the terrible Kaurava army in battle.
Tens of thousands of peacock-feathered arrows rained down on Arjuna's chariot.
Arjuna blocked the arrows with a net of arrows and sent surrounding great warriors to death.
The angry great warrior Shalya, as if playing with Arjuna in battle, shot straight crescent-headed arrows at his chest.
Arjuna cut Shalya's bow with five arrows, pierced his glove, and fiercely shot sharp arrows at his vital points.
Shalya took another heavy bow and angrily attacked Arjuna in battle.
Shalya shot three arrows at Arjuna, five at Krishna, and nine at Bhima's arms and chest.
Drona and the great warrior Shalya (King of Magadha) arrived there on Duryodhana's orders.
Young Shalya shot eight sharp arrows at Bhima who held terrible weapons.
Bhima shot ten arrows at him, then seven more, and finally shot his charioteer from the chariot seat with a crescent-headed arrow.
